There was a recent regression in btrfs/177 that started happening with
the size class patches (""btrfs: introduce size class to block group
allocator"").  This however isn't a regression introduced by those
patches
column2: but rather the bug was uncovered by a change in behavior in

column1: these patches.  The patches triggered more chunk allocations in the
^free-space-tree case
column2: which uncovered a race with device shrink.

column1: The problem is we will set the device total size to the new size
use this to find a hole for a device extent.  However during shrink we
may have device extents allocated past this range
potentially find a hole in a range past our new shrink size.  We don't
actually limit our found extent to the device size anywhere
that we will not find a hole past our device size.  This isn't true with
shrink as we're relocating block groups and thus creating holes past the
device size.
Fix this by making sure we do not search past the new device size
if we wander into any device extents that start after our device size
simply break from the loop and use whatever hole we've already found.
